title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 317: The Tragedy of the Commons and Ocean Quotas
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 317 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

The Tragedy of the Commons: Oceanic Depletion and the Illusion of Quotas

Paragraph 1. In 1968, ecologist Garrett Hardin published an influential article titled 'The Tragedy of the Commons'. Hardin argued that whenever a shared natural resource—such as a village pasture, underground water, or the open ocean—belongs to nobody, self-interested individuals will eventually ruin it. Each herdsman acts logically for personal gain: adding one more cow brings him all the profit from selling it, while the damage from overgrazing is divided among everyone. Driven by personal gain, every user keeps taking until the resource collapses.

Paragraph 2. Nowhere has this collapse appeared more clearly than in industrial ocean fishing. Over the last fifty years, giant factory ships fitted with satellite tracking, sonar fish-finders, and deep-sea nets have emptied global fish stocks. According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), over a third of commercial fisheries are currently overfished beyond safe natural limits. To stop this decline, economists promoted market-based rules called Individual Transferable Quotas (ITQs), where governments set a total catch limit and hand out tradable fishing shares like private property.

Paragraph 3. Yet in Oceans for Sale, researcher Dr. Clara Mercer challenges the real-world results of ITQs. Although quotas were promised to match business profit with nature protection, Mercer shows that rich processing companies and investment funds rapidly bought up catch shares from small independent fishers, putting national fishing fleets into corporate hands.

Paragraph 4. Furthermore, quota rules create harmful habits out at sea. Because each quota covers only one named fish species, trawler crews often practise 'high-grading'—throwing lower-quality or undersized dead fish overboard so their limited quota holds only the highest-priced fish. Accidental catches of unwanted species are also dumped back into the water. Mercer concludes that turning public oceans into private quotas does not end overfishing; it merely places marine destruction inside corporate control.

groups.title: Questions 1–5
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

groups.title: Questions 6–10
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: What was Garrett Hardin's main warning in his 1968 article?
options: A. Shared pastures always produce higher profits than private farms.
B. Governments should give free cows to struggling rural farmers.
C. Unowned shared resources are inevitably ruined by individual self-interest.
D. Underground water cannot be damaged by human farming.

steps: Đoạn 1: Tài nguyên chung không chủ sở hữu sẽ bị hủy hoại do lợi ích cá nhân.
Kết luận: Chọn C.

q2.text: Why does the author mention satellite tracking and sonar fish-finders?
options: A. To show how new technology sped up ocean fish decline
B. To prove fishing laws have successfully saved sea life
C. To explain why modern ships cost less to build
D. To argue that sonar confuses migrating sea turtles

steps: Đoạn 2: Công nghệ định vị vệ tinh và lưới kéo sâu đã làm cạn kiệt nguồn cá.
Kết luận: Chọn A.

q3.text: How does an ITQ system operate?
options: A. It forces every fishing boat to donate half its catch.
B. It permanently bans commercial fishing near coastlines.
C. It pays factory ships to stay in harbour all winter.
D. It turns national catch limits into shares companies can buy or sell.

steps: Đoạn 2: Chia hạn mức thành các suất có thể mua bán như tài sản tư nhân.
Kết luận: Chọn D.

q4.text: What problem does Dr. Mercer highlight in Paragraph 3?
options: A. Investment funds refused to spend money on ocean quotas.
B. Large corporations bought up shares and pushed out small fishers.
C. Global fish prices fell sharply after quotas began.
D. Independent fishers earned massive profits from leasing ships.

steps: Đoạn 3: Các công ty lớn mua lại hết suất của ngư dân nhỏ lẻ.
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q5.text: Why do commercial trawlers engage in 'high-grading'?
options: A. To help young fish grow larger in coastal reserves
B. To improve the water quality of deep-sea bays
C. To follow United Nations safety guidelines for ships
D. To fill their limited quota strictly with the most valuable fish

steps: Đoạn 4: Ném cá kém giá trị đi để chỉ giữ cá đắt tiền nhất cho hạn ngạch.
Kết luận: Chọn D.

q6.text: The practice of 'high-grading' causes large amounts of dead fish to be thrown back into the ocean.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...throwing lower-quality or undersized dead fish overboard..."
Kết luận: YES.

q7.text: Garrett Hardin believed that herdsmen act completely irrationally when adding extra animals.

steps: Đoạn 1: Họ hành động rất hợp lý theo lợi ích cá nhân (acts logically for personal gain), không phải vô lý.
Kết luận: NO.

q8.text: Over thirty percent of global commercial fish stocks are currently overfished.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...over a third [>33%] of commercial fisheries are currently overfished..."
Kết luận: YES.

q9.text: Dr. Clara Mercer advised European governments directly before publishing Oceans for Sale.

steps: Đoạn 3: Không hề nhắc bà có làm cố vấn cho chính phủ châu Âu hay không.
Kết luận: NOT GIVEN.

q10.text: Turning oceans into private quotas has completely solved the crisis of marine overfishing.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...does not end overfishing; it merely places marine destruction inside corporate control."
Kết luận: NO.
